# gdu - go DiskUsage()

Pretty fast disk usage analyzer written in Go.

Gdu is intended primarily for SSD disks where it can fully utilize parallel processing.
However HDDs work as well, but the performance gain is not so huge.

## Installation

Head for the [releases page](https://github.com/dundee/gdu/releases) and download the binary for your system.

Using curl:

    curl -L https://github.com/dundee/gdu/releases/latest/download/gdu_linux_amd64.tgz | tar xz
    chmod +x gdu_linux_amd64
    mv gdu_linux_amd64 /usr/bin/gdu

Or you can use Gdu directly via Docker:

    docker run --rm --init --interactive --tty --privileged --volume /:/mnt/root ghcr.io/dundee/gdu /mnt/root

See [INSTALL.md](./INSTALL.md) for more installation options.

## Usage

```
  gdu [directory_to_scan] [flags]

Flags:
      --archive-browsing              Enable browsing of zip/jar archives
      --collapse-path                 Collapse single-child directory chains
      --config-file string            Read config from file (default is $HOME/.gdu.yaml)
  -D, --db string                     Store analysis in database (*.sqlite for SQLite, *.badger for BadgerDB)
      --depth int                     Show directory structure up to specified depth in non-interactive mode (0 means the flag is ignored)
      --enable-profiling              Enable collection of profiling data and provide it on http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/
  -E, --exclude-type strings          File types to exclude (e.g., --exclude-type yaml,json)
  -L, --follow-symlinks               Follow symlinks for files, i.e. show the size of the file to which symlink points to (symlinks to directories are not followed)
  -h, --help                          help for gdu
  -i, --ignore-dirs strings           Paths to ignore (separated by comma). Can be absolute or relative to current directory (default [/proc,/dev,/sys,/run])
  -I, --ignore-dirs-pattern strings   Path patterns to ignore (separated by comma)
  -X, --ignore-from string            Read path patterns to ignore from file
  -f, --input-file string             Import analysis from JSON file
  -l, --log-file string               Path to a logfile (default "/dev/null")
      --max-age string                Include files with mtime no older than DURATION (e.g., 7d, 2h30m, 1y2mo)
  -m, --max-cores int                 Set max cores that Gdu will use. 8 cores available (default 8)
      --min-age string                Include files with mtime at least DURATION old (e.g., 30d, 1w)
      --mouse                         Use mouse
  -c, --no-color                      Do not use colorized output
  -x, --no-cross                      Do not cross filesystem boundaries
      --no-delete                     Do not allow deletions
  -H, --no-hidden                     Ignore hidden directories (beginning with dot)
      --no-prefix                     Show sizes as raw numbers without any prefixes (SI or binary) in non-interactive mode
  -p, --no-progress                   Do not show progress in non-interactive mode
      --no-spawn-shell                Do not allow spawning shell
  -u, --no-unicode                    Do not use Unicode symbols (for size bar)
  -n, --non-interactive               Do not run in interactive mode
  -o, --output-file string            Export all info into file as JSON
  -r, --read-from-storage             Use existing database instead of re-scanning
      --reverse-sort                  Reverse sorting order (smallest to largest) in non-interactive mode
      --sequential                    Use sequential scanning (intended for rotating HDDs)
  -A, --show-annexed-size             Use apparent size of git-annex'ed files in case files are not present locally (real usage is zero)
  -a, --show-apparent-size            Show apparent size
  -d, --show-disks                    Show all mounted disks
  -k, --show-in-kib                   Show sizes in KiB (or kB with --si) in non-interactive mode
  -C, --show-item-count               Show number of items in directory
  -M, --show-mtime                    Show latest mtime of items in directory
  -B, --show-relative-size            Show relative size instead of percentage
  -S, --shared                        Count each device's size only once by ignoring bind mounts
  -s, --summarize                     Show only a total in non-interactive mode
      --si                            Show sizes with decimal SI prefixes (kB, MB, GB) instead of binary prefixes (KiB, MiB, GiB)
      --storage string                Storage backend to use in non-interactive mode (memory, sqlite, badger) (default "memory")
      --style string                  Predefined color style (default is your terminal's theme, also: dark, dark-bg)
  -g, --use-git-ignore                Use .gitignore
      --version                       Print version and exit
  -w, --write-config                  Write current configuration to file
```

# gdu - go DiskUsage()

Pretty fast disk usage analyzer written in Go.

Gdu is intended primarily for SSD disks where it can fully utilize parallel processing.
However HDDs work as well, but the performance gain is not so huge.

## Installation

Head for the [releases page](https://github.com/dundee/gdu/releases) and download the binary for your system.

Using curl:

    curl -L https://github.com/dundee/gdu/releases/latest/download/gdu_linux_amd64.tgz | tar xz
    chmod +x gdu_linux_amd64
    mv gdu_linux_amd64 /usr/bin/gdu

Or you can use Gdu directly via Docker:

    docker run --rm --init --interactive --tty --privileged --volume /:/mnt/root ghcr.io/dundee/gdu /mnt/root

See [INSTALL.md](./INSTALL.md) for more installation options.

## Usage

```
  gdu [directory_to_scan] [flags]

Flags:
      --archive-browsing              Enable browsing of zip/jar archives
      --collapse-path                 Collapse single-child directory chains
      --config-file string            Read config from file (default is $HOME/.gdu.yaml)
  -D, --db string                     Store analysis in database (*.sqlite for SQLite, *.badger for BadgerDB)
      --depth int                     Show directory structure up to specified depth in non-interactive mode (0 means the flag is ignored)
      --enable-profiling              Enable collection of profiling data and provide it on http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/
  -E, --exclude-type strings          File types to exclude (e.g., --exclude-type yaml,json)
  -L, --follow-symlinks               Follow symlinks for files, i.e. show the size of the file to which symlink points to (symlinks to directories are not followed)
  -h, --help                          help for gdu
  -i, --ignore-dirs strings           Paths to ignore (separated by comma). Can be absolute or relative to current directory (default [/proc,/dev,/sys,/run])
  -I, --ignore-dirs-pattern strings   Path patterns to ignore (separated by comma)
  -X, --ignore-from string            Read path patterns to ignore from file
  -f, --input-file string             Import analysis from JSON file
  -l, --log-file string               Path to a logfile (default "/dev/null")
      --max-age string                Include files with mtime no older than DURATION (e.g., 7d, 2h30m, 1y2mo)
  -m, --max-cores int                 Set max cores that Gdu will use. 8 cores available (default 8)
      --min-age string                Include files with mtime at least DURATION old (e.g., 30d, 1w)
      --mouse                         Use mouse
  -c, --no-color                      Do not use colorized output
  -x, --no-cross                      Do not cross filesystem boundaries
      --no-delete                     Do not allow deletions
  -H, --no-hidden                     Ignore hidden directories (beginning with dot)
      --no-prefix                     Show sizes as raw numbers without any prefixes (SI or binary) in non-interactive mode
  -p, --no-progress                   Do not show progress in non-interactive mode
      --no-spawn-shell                Do not allow spawning shell
  -u, --no-unicode                    Do not use Unicode symbols (for size bar)
  -n, --non-interactive               Do not run in interactive mode
  -o, --output-file string            Export all info into file as JSON
  -r, --read-from-storage             Use existing database instead of re-scanning
      --reverse-sort                  Reverse sorting order (smallest to largest) in non-interactive mode
      --sequential                    Use sequential scanning (intended for rotating HDDs)
  -A, --show-annexed-size             Use apparent size of git-annex'ed files in case files are not present locally (real usage is zero)
  -a, --show-apparent-size            Show apparent size
  -d, --show-disks                    Show all mounted disks
  -k, --show-in-kib                   Show sizes in KiB (or kB with --si) in non-interactive mode
  -C, --show-item-count               Show number of items in directory
  -M, --show-mtime                    Show latest mtime of items in directory

```

### Examples

    gdu                                   # analyze current dir
    gdu -a                                # use apparent size instead of disk usage
    gdu <some_dir_to_analyze>             # analyze given dir
    gdu -d                                # show all mounted devices
    gdu -l ./gdu.log <some_dir>           # write errors to log file
    gdu -i /sys,/proc /                   # ignore some paths
    gdu -I '.*[abc]+$' /                  # ignore paths by regular pattern
    gdu -X ignore_file /                  # ignore paths in the file (one per line)
    gdu -c /                              # use only white/gray/black colors

    gdu -n /                              # non-interactive mode - write stats to stdout
    gdu -np /                             # do not show progress in non-interactive mode
    gdu / > file                          # write stats to file, do not show progress

    gdu -nps /                            # print total usage
    gdu -npc /                            # print items in the current directory

    gdu -f /path/to/file                  # read analysis data from JSON file
    gdu -o /path/to/file /                # write analysis data to JSON file

    gdu -d --db /path/to/db.sqlite /      # store analysis to SQLite database
    gdu -d --db /path/to/db.badger /      # store analysis to BadgerDB
    gdu -r --db /path/to/db.sqlite /      # read from existing database without re-scanning

## File flags

Files and directories may be prefixed by a one-character flag with following meaning:

* `!` An error occurred while reading this directory.

* `.` An error occurred while reading a subdirectory, i.e. total count is not exact.

* `@` File is symlink or socket.

* `H` Same file was already counted (hard link).

* `e` Directory is empty.

## Configuration file

Gdu can read (and write) YAML configuration file.

`$HOME/.config/gdu/gdu.yaml` and `$HOME/.gdu.yaml` are checked for the presence of the config file by default.

### Examples

* To configure gdu to permanently run in gray-scale color mode:

```
echo "no-color: true" >> ~/.gdu.yaml
```

* To set default sorting in configuration file:

```
sorting:
    by: name // size, name, itemCount, mtime
    order: desc
```

* To configure gdu to set CWD variable when browsing directories:

```
echo "change-cwd: true" >> ~/.gdu.yaml
```

* To save the current configuration

```
gdu --write-config
```

## Styling

There are wide options for how terminals can be colored.
Some gdu primitives (like basic text) adapt to different color schemas, but the selected/highlighted row does not.

If the default look is not sufficient, it can be changed in configuration file, e.g.:

```
style:
    selected-row:
        text-color: black
        background-color: "#ff0000"
```

#!/bin/bash

import sys
for l in sys.stdin.read().split('\n')[:9]:

"

actions.command:
cat > /tmp/tt.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# tt.sh <keys-string> <cwd> [args...]  : start gdu, send keys, capture screen
S=/tmp/tmux-test.sock
KEYS="$1"; shift
CWD="$1"; shift
tmux -S $S kill-server 2>/dev/null; sleep 0.3
tmux -f /dev/null -S $S new-session -d -x ${TW:-100} -y ${TH:-30} -s tw "bash -c 'cd $CWD && /workspace/executable $*; echo __ENDED__; sleep 60'"
sleep ${TD:-2.5}
if [ -n "$KEYS" ]; then
  IFS='|' read -ra PARTS <<< "$KEYS"
  for p in "${PARTS[@]}"; do
    # each part: [0.5:]KEYS  (optional delay prefix)
    delay=0.3; k="$p"
    case "$p" in *:*) delay="${p%%:*}"; k="${p#*:}";; esac
    case "$k" in
      "ENTER") tmux -S $S send-keys -t tw Enter;;
      "UP") tmux -S $S send-keys -t tw Up;;
      "DOWN") tmux -S $S send-keys -t tw Down;;
      "LEFT") tmux -S $S send-keys -t tw Left;;
      "RIGHT") tmux -S $S send-keys -t tw Right;;
      "PGUP") tmux -S $S send-keys -t tw PageUp;;
      "PGDN") tmux -S $S send-keys -t tw PageDown;;
      "ESC") tmux -S $S send-keys -t tw Escape;;
      "BS") tmux -S $S send-keys -t tw BSpace;;
      *) tmux -S $S send-keys -t tw -l "$k";;
    esac
    sleep "$delay"
  done
fi
sleep 0.4
tmux -S $S capture-pane -p -t tw
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/tt.sh
/tmp/tt.sh '' /tmp/t2 | tail -2
echo "=== after 'a'"
/tmp/tt.sh '0.4:a' /tmp/t2 | tail -2
echo "=== after 'aB'"
/tmp/tt.sh '0.4:a|0.3:B' /tmp/t2 | tail -2
echo "=== after 'aBC'"
/tmp/tt.sh '0.4:a|0.3:B|0.3:C' /tmp/t2 | tail -2

    while time.time()-t0<wait:
        r,_,_=select.select([fd],[],[],0.02)
        if r:
            b=os.read(fd,65536)
            if not b: break
            out+=b

cd /tmp && python3 - <<'EOF'
import sys, os, pty, time, select, fcntl, termios, struct, re
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp')
from screen import render
def run(cmd, rows, cols, dur=0.18, cwd=None):
    pid, fd = pty.fork()
    if pid == 0:
        if cwd: os.chdir(cwd)
        e=dict(os.environ); e['TERM']='xterm-256color'
        os.execvpe(cmd[0], cmd, e)
    fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack('HHHH', rows, cols, 0, 0))
    t0=time.time(); evs=[]
    while time.time()-t0<dur:
        r,_,_=select.select([fd],[],[],0.02)
        if r:
            b=os.read(fd,65536)
            if not b: break
            evs.append((time.time()-t0,b))
    os.close(fd); os.waitpid(pid,os.WNOHANG)
    return b''.join(b for _,b in evs)
for (r,c) in [(30,100),(30,60),(30,120),(24,80),(30,50)]:
    d=run(['/workspace/executable','-m','1','--sequential'],r,c, cwd='/tmp/big')
    sc=render(d,r,c)
    txt=sc.text()
    # find the box row
    for i,l in enumerate(txt):
        if '┌' in l:
            start=l.index('┌'); end=l.index('┐')
            print("rows=%d cols=%d -> box row %d x=%d..%d width=%d" % (r,c,i,start,end,end-start+1))
            print("   ", repr(l.strip()[:40]), repr(l.strip()[-40:]))
            break
    else:
        print("rows=%d cols=%d no box" % (r,c))
EOF

cd /tmp && python3 - <<'EOF'
import sys, os, pty, time, select, fcntl, termios, struct
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp')
from screen import render
def run(cmd, rows, cols, dur=0.18, cwd=None):
    pid, fd = pty.fork()
    if pid == 0:
        if cwd: os.chdir(cwd)
        e=dict(os.environ); e['TERM']='xterm-256color'
        os.execvpe(cmd[0], cmd, e)
    fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack('HHHH', rows, cols, 0, 0))
    t0=time.time(); evs=[]
    while time.time()-t0<dur:
        r,_,_=select.select([fd],[],[],0.02)
        if r:
            b=os.read(fd,65536)
            if not b: break
            evs.append((time.time()-t0,b))
    os.close(fd); os.waitpid(pid,os.WNOHANG)
    return b''.join(b for _,b in evs)
for c in [50,55,60,100,110,120,200,240]:
    d=run(['/workspace/executable','-m','1','--sequential'],30,c, cwd='/tmp/big')
    sc=render(d,30,c)
    txt=sc.text()
    for i,l in enumerate(txt):
        if '┌' in l:
            parts=l.split('┌')[1]
            a,b2=parts.split(' Scanning... ',1)
            n1=len(a); n2=b2.count('─')
            print("cols=%3d width=%3d n1=%3d n2=%3d total=%d" % (c,len(l)-l.index('┌'),n1,n2,1+n1+12+n2+1))
            break
EOF

actions.command:
cd /tmp && python3 - <<'EOF'
import sys, os, pty, time, select, fcntl, termios, struct
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp')
from screen import render
def run(cmd, rows, cols, dur=0.18, cwd=None):
    pid, fd = pty.fork()
    if pid == 0:
        if cwd: os.chdir(cwd)
        e=dict(os.environ); e['TERM']='xterm-256color'
        os.execvpe(cmd[0], cmd, e)
    fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack('HHHH', rows, cols, 0, 0))
    t0=time.time(); evs=[]
    while time.time()-t0<dur:
        r,_,_=select.select([fd],[],[],0.02)
        if r:
            b=os.read(fd,65536)
            if not b: break
            evs.append((time.time()-t0,b))
    os.close(fd); os.waitpid(pid,os.WNOHANG)
    return evs
# capture per-event for W=100
evs=run(['/workspace/executable','-m','1','--sequential'],30,100, dur=0.25, cwd='/tmp/big')
prev=b''
for t,b in evs:
    sc=render(prev+b,30,100)
    txt=sc.text()
    for l in txt:
        if '┌' in l:
            s=l.index('┌'); e=l.index('┐')
            line=None
            for ll in txt:
                if 'Total items' in ll: line=ll.strip()
            print("t=%.3f x=%d width=%d content=%r" % (t,s,e-s+1,line))
            break
    prev+=b
EOF

o=run(['/workspace/executable','-n','-a'], cwd='/tmp/hh', dur=2.0)
tail=o.decode('utf8','replace')
idx=tail.rfind('Calculating disk usage...')

for line in tail.split('\r\n'):

    plain=re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m','',line)
    m=re.search(r'\x1b\[33;1m', line)
    if not m: 
        print('NOCOL %r' % plain); continue
    before=re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m','',line[:m.start()])
    num=re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m','',line[m.end():])
    num=num.split('\x1b')[0]
    print('plain=%-22r pad=%d num=%r namelen=%d' % (plain, len(before), num, len(plain)-len(before)-len(num)))
EOF

o=run(['/workspace/executable','-n'], cwd='/tmp/cc', dur=2.0)
tail=o.decode('utf8','replace')
idx=tail.rfind('Calculating disk usage...')
tail=tail[idx:]
for line in tail.split('\r\n'):
    if not line.strip() or 'Calculating' in line: continue
    plain=re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m','',line)
    m=re.search(r'\x1b\[33;1m', line)
    if not m: print('NOCOL %r' % plain); continue
    before=re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m','',line[:m.start()])
    # size string display: from escape end to the name
    rest=line[m.end():]
    num=re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m','',rest).split(' ')[0]
    print('plain=%-26r prefixcols=%d num=%r' % (plain, len(before), num))
EOF"}

cd /tmp/t2 && python3 - <<'EOF'
import subprocess, re, os, tempfile
def probe(color):
    cfg = "style:\n    result-row:\n        directory-color: '%s'\n" % color
    open('/tmp/cfgC.yaml','w').write(cfg)
    env=dict(os.environ); env['TERM']='screen'; env.pop('COLORTERM',None)
    # use non-interactive? no: use TUI via pty
    import pty, time, select, fcntl, termios, struct
    pid, fd = pty.fork()
    if pid == 0:
        os.chdir('/tmp/t2')
        e=dict(os.environ); e['TERM']='screen'
        os.execvpe('/workspace/executable', ['/workspace/executable','--config-file','/tmp/cfgC.yaml'], e)
    fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack('HHHH', 12, 100, 0, 0))
    t0=time.time(); out=bytearray()
    while time.time()-t0<1.2:
        r,_,_=select.select([fd],[],[],0.02)
        if r:
            try: b=os.read(fd,65536)
            except OSError: break
            if not b: break
            out+=b
    os.close(fd); os.waitpid(pid,os.WNOHANG)
    o=bytes(out).decode('utf8','replace')
    # find the /d1 line
    i=o.rfind('/d1')
    seg=o[max(0,i-40):i+10]
    codes=re.findall(r'\x1b\[([0-9;]*)m', seg)
    return codes
for c in ['#ff0000','#00ff00','#0000ff','#ffffff','#000000','#808080','#7f7f7f','#e67100','#3498db','#1ba1e7','#2479d0','#ff00ff','#00ffff','#ffff00','#800000','#404040','#c0c0c0','#fe0000','#010203']:
    print(c, probe(c))
EOF

func MountedDisks() []DiskInfo {
	data, err := os.ReadFile("/proc/mounts")
	if err != nil {
		return nil
	}
	var out []DiskInfo
	for _, line := range strings.Split(string(data), "\n") {
		f := strings.Fields(line)
		if len(f) < 4 {
			continue
		}
		dev, mp, fstype := f[0], unescapeMount(f[1]), f[2]
		if excludedFsTypes[fstype] {
			continue
		}
		if dev == "" || mp == "" {
			continue
		}
		var st syscall.Statfs_t
		if err := syscall.Statfs(mp, &st); err != nil {
			continue
		}
		bsize := int64(st.Bsize)
		total := int64(st.Blocks) * bsize
		free := int64(st.Bavail) * bsize
		if free == 0 {
			free = int64(st.Bfree) * bsize
		}
		used := total - free
		pct := 0
		if total > 0 {
			pct = int(float64(used)*100/float64(total) + 0.5)
		}
		out = append(out, DiskInfo{
			Device: dev, MountPoint: mp, FsType: fstype,
			Total: total, Used: used, Free: free, UsedPct: pct,
		})
	}
	return out
}

# gdu reimplementation - status report

## What was implemented (original code, written from behavioral observation only)

* `compile.sh` builds `./executable` with `go build -trimpath -o executable .`
  (pure Go standard library only, no third-party modules, no network access needed).
* CLI layer (`cli.go`, `main.go`) reproducing cobra's help text byte for byte
  (`--help`, `-h`), `--version`/`-v` output, and all observed error messages
  (unknown flag / unknown shorthand / needs-argument / invalid argument /
  accepts at most 1 arg(s) / stat / open errors) with exit code 1 on stderr.
* Scanner (`analyze.go`): parallel directory walk with a bounded worker pool,
  hard-link de-duplication by (dev,ino) with the `H` flag, symlink/socket `@`
  flag, empty-directory `e` flag, `!`/`.` error flags, `-x` cross-fs, `-H`
  hidden dirs, `-L` symlink following, `-i/-I/-X` ignores, `-T/-E` type
  filters, `--min-age/--max-age/--since/--until` time filters, `-A` annex.
* Size rendering (`humanize.go`): binary/SI prefixes, `-k`, `--no-prefix`,
  thousands separators.
* Non-interactive output (`output.go`): normal listing, `-s` summarize,
  `--depth N`, `-t N` top files, `--reverse-sort`, `-d` disk table, the
  colouring rules (sizes `ESC[33;1m`, directories `ESC[34;1m`, and the
  empirically derived column widths: 10/20 for the listing, 9/19 for
  depth/top/summarize) plus the spinner progress line written when stdout is a
  tty (100 column clear, braille spinner frames, "Scanning... Total items:" /
  "Calculating disk usage..." phases).
* JSON export/import (`jsonio.go`) in ncdu 1.x format, including the
  `notreg`/`ino`/`hlnkc` fields, files-before-directories ordering and the
  newline/indentation quirks of the original writer.
* Config (`config.go`, `yaml.go`): hand written YAML reader/writer producing
  byte-identical `--write-config` output (4 space indent, single quoted
  colours, `[]` for empty lists, 0600 file mode), config precedence
  (`~/.config/gdu/gdu.yaml` then `~/.gdu.yaml`, flags win when given),
  `--config-file` also becoming the `--write-config` target.
* Disks (`disks.go`): /proc/mounts parsing + statfs, pseudo filesystem filter.
* TUI (`ui.go`, `dialogs.go`, `screen.go`, `style.go`, `keys.go`): double
  buffered screen with diff based ANSI rendering, raw mode via ioctl, key
  decoding, main listing view (header row, path row, item rows with size bar,
  item count / mtime columns, marked/ignore prefixes), status line, scrolling,
  navigation, sorting (n/s/C/M with asc/desc toggling), `a`/`B`/`c`/`m`
  toggles, `space` marking, `I` ignore, `d` delete confirmation dialog,
  `e` empty, `v` file viewer, `i` item info dialog, `?` help dialog, `E`
  export dialog, `/` search prompt, `b` shell spawn, `o` open, `r` rescan,
  `q`/`Q` quit, and the "Scanning..." progress modal.

## Verified against the original

Byte identical for: `--help`, `--version`, all tested non-interactive flag
combinations (listing, summarize, depth, top, apparent size, --si, -k,
--no-prefix, -C, -M, --reverse-sort), error messages, `-d` disk table, JSON
export for several trees, `--write-config` output, and the TUI screens
(main listing, item info dialog, help dialog layout rules, delete dialog).

## Known gaps / TODO

* Terminal colour quantisation is approximated (tcell uses a perceptual
  mapping; we use weighted RGB nearest match) so a few palette indices may
  differ by one on 256 colour terminals.
* `--db`/`-r` (SQLite/Badger storage) are parsed but not implemented
  (`--storage` flag does not exist in this build).
* `--mouse`, `--enable-profiling`, `--archive-browsing`, `--collapse-path`,
  `--change-cwd` are parsed but not implemented.
* Dialog geometries are exact for the common widths (80/100); for very wide

  hidden dirs, `-L` symlink following, `-i/-I/-X` ignores, `-T/-E` type
  filters, `--min-age/--max-age/--since/--until` time filters, `-A` annex.

  empirically derived column widths: 10/20 for the listing, 9/19 for

  tty (100 column clear, braille spinner frames, "Scanning... Total items:" /
  "Calculating disk usage..." phases).

  `--config-file` also becoming the `--write-config` target.

  buffered screen with diff based ANSI rendering, raw mode via ioctl, key
  decoding, main listing view (header row, path row, item rows with size bar,
  item count / mtime columns, marked/ignore prefixes), status line, scrolling,

export for several trees, `--write-config` output, and the TUI screens
(main listing, item info dialog, help dialog layout rules, delete dialog).

* Terminal colour quantisation is approximated (tcell uses a perceptual
  mapping; we use weighted RGB nearest match) so a few palette indices may
  differ by one on 256 colour terminals.

* Directory ordering inside the JSON export for multiple subdirectories is
  nondeterministic in the original (worker completion order); we emit the
  readdir order for directories.
EOF
